findings.summary: A project's readiness is the restricted report's own metrics, with a site-weighted metric, instead of a second kind partition and a duplicated declaration count.
The adapter census follows the referenced functions and probes only them, so a project report no longer pays for every exported function.
The pin gap is read from the import structure in the usage scan against the surface's entry, not from diagnostic message text.
Receipts, collection runs and reports share one coverage directory; a project report nests under projects/<directory>-<entry>.
Stale or missing evidence is stated in the readiness and on the console instead of appearing as zero support; the --run conflict is checked at parse time.
The entry is resolved once, the restriction is a positional flag, the helpers use the named surface and usage types, and optional blocks are plain undefined.
The help line is generated from the same flag table the parser reads.
The page embeds no export table or file digests, and the readiness paragraph is a sibling element rather than a nested paragraph.
The test shares one baseline helper, checks the embedded pin gap instead of a literal present in every page, and drops the assertion its neighbour subsumed.
The documentation says the entry is scanned against this repository's pin and that receipts must be collected at the current inputs.
